papers.title: A Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD) pipeline via DRUG-GAN: A multiscale method for drug-like/target-specific compound library generation.
papers.abstract: We present the Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a deep learning-driven pipeline for efficient drug lead identification. FSGLD integrates generative modeling with molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, ligand-residue interaction profile, MM-PBSA, thermodynamic integration (TI), and experimental validation to bridge theoretical design and practical application. The core multiscale DRUG-GAN models enable generative model-guided discovery of drug-like and target-specific compounds across three scenarios: (i) generation of random drug-like compounds, (ii) generation of t
papers.summary: The authors present FSGLD, a deep learning pipeline that combines a generative adversarial network (DRUG-GAN) with a cascade of physics-based validation steps—docking, molecular dynamics, MM-PBSA, and thermodynamic integration—plus experimental testing to discover drug-like and target-specific compounds. The multiscale approach aims to bridge computational design and practical lead identification across three generation scenarios. It represents an integrated workflow rather than a single novel model.

papers.title: Ebola Virus VP40 C-terminal Lysine Residue Mediates Lipid Interactions and Dimer-Dimer Interactions.
papers.abstract: The Ebola virus (EBOV) matrix protein VP40 is the main driver of viral assembly and budding, processes which depend on its ability to oligomerize at the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane (PM). VP40 forms dimers in the cytoplasm that traffic to the membrane and assemble into higher-order oligomers, but the specific molecular determinants governing the stability of these oligomeric interfaces are not fully understood. Here, we investigate the role of the C-terminal lysine residue, Lys326, in mediating VP40-lipid and VP40-VP40 interactions. Using a combination of molecular dynamics simulations
papers.summary: This study investigates how a single C-terminal lysine residue (Lys326) in the Ebola virus matrix protein VP40 contributes to the protein's ability to bind lipid membranes and to assemble into higher-order oligomers. Using molecular dynamics simulations, the authors show that Lys326 mediates both VP40-lipid interactions and dimer-dimer contacts, helping explain how VP40 assembles and buds at the plasma membrane.

papers.title: Identification of a novel equine rotavirus B from Missouri in 2025, which is distantly related to group B rotaviruses.
papers.abstract: Despite the wide circulation of group B rotaviruses in animals and humans, rotavirus B was not found in horses until 2021 in Kentucky, USA. Little is known about the genetic diversity and evolution of rotavirus B in this new host. Here, we described a divergent equine rotavirus B (ERVB) from a foal with idiopathic diarrhea in Missouri (designated MO-ERVB-25). Full-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis revealed that MO-ERVB-25 is distantly related to all previously known group B rotaviruses, including ERVB strains identified in 2021 in Kentucky (KY-ERVB-21). The mean nucleotide substituti
papers.summary: Researchers identified and sequenced a novel equine rotavirus B (MO-ERVB-25) from a foal with diarrhea in Missouri in 2025. Full-genome phylogenetic analysis showed it is genetically distinct from all previously known group B rotaviruses, including the first equine strains found in Kentucky in 2021, indicating substantial unrecognized diversity and ongoing evolution of rotavirus B in horses.

papers.title: Harnessing engineered laccase and functional carrier materials for efficient dye degradation: From mechanism to application.
papers.abstract: Laccases are copper-containing oxidases that have been widely investigated for the decolorization and degradation of synthetic dyes, including azo, anthraquinone, triphenylmethane, indigo and thiazine dyes. However, their application in dye-containing wastewater remains constrained by enzyme instability under complex effluent conditions, limited oxidation of some recalcitrant or high-redox-potential dyes, mediator dependence, and poor recovery and reuse of free laccase. This review discusses recent progress in laccase-catalyzed dye degradation from a mechanism-to-engineering perspective, linki
papers.summary: This review examines recent advances in using laccase enzymes, combined with engineered carrier materials, to degrade synthetic dyes in wastewater. It covers the catalytic mechanisms of laccase across dye classes and discusses engineering strategies—such as immobilization on functional materials and mediator systems—to overcome enzyme instability, limited substrate range, and poor reusability. The work bridges mechanistic understanding with practical application design for bioremediation.

papers.title: A critical review of degradation pathways and stability engineering for high-efficiency non-fullerene acceptor-based organic solar cells via multiscale computational approaches.
papers.abstract: The emergence of non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) has significantly transformed the landscape of organic solar cells (OSCs) and paved the way for achieving unprecedented power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) and making them suitable for practical photovoltaic applications. Computational techniques, meanwhile, have become essential for the efficient discovery, screening, and optimization of new photovoltaic (PV) materials. This review gives a comprehensive summary of the recent developments in computational design and construction of NFAs with special attention to the use of computational tools in
papers.summary: This review surveys computational approaches for designing non-fullerene acceptors in organic solar cells, with a focus on degradation pathways and stability engineering. It covers how multiscale modeling tools are used to screen, optimize, and predict the stability of photovoltaic materials. The paper is a broad overview rather than a new experimental or methodological result.

papers.title: Brominated 1,4-dihydropyridine derivatives as potential insecticides against the cotton aphid (Aphis gossypii): synthesis, characterization, biological evaluation, and molecular docking studies.
papers.abstract: A new series of brominated 1,4-dihydropyridine derivatives bearing various aryl and heteroaryl substituents was successfully synthesized through a microwave-assisted multicomponent Hantzsch reaction followed by bromination under solar irradiation. The synthesized compounds were characterized by IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR spectroscopy and elemental analyses. Their insecticidal activities were evaluated against adult and nymphal stages of the cotton aphid, Aphis gossypii, using the leaf-dipping bioassay technique. Biological evaluation demonstrated that all synthesized derivatives exhibited significant
papers.summary: Researchers synthesized a new series of brominated 1,4-dihydropyridine compounds using microwave-assisted multicomponent reactions and solar-irradiation bromination, then tested them against the cotton aphid (Aphis gossypii). All derivatives showed significant insecticidal activity against adult and nymphal aphids in leaf-dipping bioassays, with molecular docking used to probe the binding mode. The work identifies a new class of potential aphid-control agents.

papers.title: On the limits of marginal protein folding stability: methodological goals and drawbacks.
papers.abstract: Why do proteins remain at the edge of stability rather than evolving toward maximal thermodynamic robustness? Can we trust the computational methods that inform about when and how stability falls off that edge? Marginal stability, the confinement of protein folding free energies to a window of approximately 5-15 kcal/mol, is broadly observed in biophysics, and its mechanistic causes, involving evolutionary and biophysical properties, remain under debate and require accurate predictions. In this regard, protein folding stability is currently predicted using both traditional structure-based homo
papers.summary: This paper examines why proteins evolve to be only marginally stable (folding free energies of ~5–15 kcal/mol) rather than maximally stable, and critically evaluates the computational methods used to predict folding stability. It discusses the methodological goals and limitations of structure-based approaches for estimating when and how stability falls off this marginal edge.

papers.title: Substrate recognition and stage-dependent transformation of aflatoxin B1 by mediator-free Bacillus laccase frL103.
papers.abstract: Enzyme-based mitigation of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is commonly evaluated by parent-toxin depletion. This study characterized the stage-dependent, mediator-free transformation of AFB1 by recombinant Bacillus laccase frL103 and assessed chemical, biological, and structural outcomes. UHPLC-HRMS profiling at 0, 30, and 60 h yielded 2846 filtered features and showed that the AFB1 response decreased to 23.8% and 14.8% of the initial value at 30 and 60 h, respectively. A feature at m/z 329.0660 increased at 30 h and declined to 17.7% of that response at 60 h; accurate mass and MS/MS fragmentation support
papers.summary: This study characterizes how a mediator-free Bacillus laccase (frL103) transforms aflatoxin B1 over time, showing that the parent toxin drops to ~24% and ~15% of initial levels at 30 and 60 hours. A transient intermediate feature (m/z 329.0660) rises at 30 h then declines, indicating stage-dependent transformation rather than simple depletion. The work highlights that parent-toxin loss alone is an incomplete measure of detoxification.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Relative Ligand Binding Free Energy Simulation Methods: Amber-TI, GROMACS-NETI, OpenMM-FEP, and BLaDE-MSLD.
papers.abstract: Structure-based drug design has become increasingly important in the pharmaceutical industry for accelerating the discovery of effective drug candidates. In particular, ligand binding free energy serves as a critical metric for predicting drug efficacy during the key stages of hit discovery and lead optimization. Continuous progress has been made in the prediction of ligand binding free energies, but direct comparisons of different methods using the same force field remain challenging due to their unique implementations in different simulation engines. In this study, we present a direct compar
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: This study directly compares four relative ligand binding free energy simulation methods—Amber-TI, GROMACS-NETI, OpenMM-FEP, and BLaDE-MSLD—using the same force field to isolate methodological differences from implementation effects. The authors assess accuracy and efficiency across the methods, providing a rare head-to-head benchmark for structure-based drug design workflows. The work helps clarify which free energy approaches are most reliable and practical for hit discovery and lead optimization.

papers.title: SynBioFooDB: a comprehensive resource for synthetic biology-driven food biomanufacturing.
papers.abstract: Enabled by synthetic biology and metabolic engineering, microbial biomanufacturing is reshaping the production of food-related compounds by offering sustainable alternatives to resource-intensive extraction and conventional chemical synthesis. However, information linking food-related compounds to biosynthetic pathways and microbial biomanufacturing evidence remains fragmented across the literature and poorly represented in existing food-oriented resources, hindering cross-study comparison, evidence synthesis, and rational design of microbial production systems. Here, we present SynBioFooDB (h
papers.summary: SynBioFooDB is a new database that consolidates information on food-related compounds, their biosynthetic pathways, and evidence for microbial biomanufacturing, addressing the fragmentation of this knowledge across literature and existing food resources. It aims to enable cross-study comparison, evidence synthesis, and rational design of microbial production systems for food compounds.

papers.title: Single-Chain Conformational Fluctuation Regulates Phase Separation of Intrinsically Disordered Proteins.
papers.abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) form biomolecular condensates through weak multivalent interactions, but the ensemble variables that control condensate stability and material properties remain incompletely defined. Most current descriptions emphasize sequence features or mean single-chain descriptors, such as the radius of gyration R g. Here, we ask whether the breadth of the single-chain ensemble can regulate liquid-liquid phase separation when the amino-acid sequence and mean chain size are fixed. We develop an all-atom-informed maximum-entropy coarse-grained model of the low-comple
papers.summary: This study uses an all-atom-informed maximum-entropy coarse-grained model to show that, even when amino-acid sequence and mean chain size (radius of gyration) are held fixed, the breadth of the single-chain conformational ensemble can regulate whether and how intrinsically disordered proteins undergo liquid-liquid phase separation. The work identifies conformational fluctuation—not just sequence or average size—as a tunable variable controlling condensate stability and material properties.

papers.title: Computational Design Strategies for Nanoscale 3D Auxetic Metastructures from DNA.
papers.abstract: Auxetic metamaterials exhibit negative Poisson's ratio (NPR) behaviors due to their architecture of periodically arranged unit cells. Although mechanical metamaterials are well established at the macroscale, programmable auxetic units remain scarce at the nanoscale. DNA origami offers a promising platform to bridge this gap, but design principles for dynamically deformable 3D auxetic nanostructures remain largely unexplored. Here, we develop design strategies for such 3D auxetic metastructures built from wireframe DNA origami. As a model system, we use a 3D re-entrant triangular unit composed
papers.summary: This paper develops computational design strategies for nanoscale 3D auxetic (negative Poisson's ratio) metastructures built from wireframe DNA origami, using a re-entrant triangular unit cell as a model system. It addresses the gap between well-established macroscale mechanical metamaterials and the scarcity of programmable auxetic units at the nanoscale, providing design principles for dynamically deformable 3D auxetic nanostructures.

papers.title: Mapping Functional Transitions across Protein Homologues from a Single Simulation: Application of gEDES-HM to Adenylate Kinases.
papers.abstract: Proteins fluctuate across different conformational states, which constitute a dynamic ensemble that regulates their interaction networks and functions. Predicting the conformational landscape remains a computational challenge, and even more difficult is capturing the link between state distributions and specific functions within protein homologues. Here, we present gEDES-HM (generalized Ensemble Docking with Enhanced sampling of pocket Shape-Homology Modeling), a scalable computational protocol enabling us to remap conformational ensembles obtained from enhanced sampling simulations of a singl
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors introduce gEDES-HM, a computational protocol that uses enhanced sampling simulations of a single protein to generate conformational ensembles for its homologues via homology modeling and pocket-shape docking. Applied to adenylate kinases, it maps functional transitions across the family from one simulation, linking state distributions to function. This offers a scalable way to predict conformational landscapes and functional differences among related proteins.

papers.title: Molecular insights into GPR55 modulation reveal an atypical activation mechanism and glycosylation-dependent efficacy regulation.
papers.abstract: GPR55 is a lipid-activated G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) implicated in metabolism, inflammation, and neurodegeneration. Lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) species are proposed as endogenous agonists, but progress in understanding GPR55 function has still been limited by suboptimal chemical probes. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of GPR55 in both inactive and active states. The inactive-state structure bound to the inverse agonist CID16020046 facilitated the rational design of an improved in vitro tool compound, BI-8310. Surprisingly, mutation of a glycosylation s
papers.summary: The authors solved cryo-EM structures of the lipid receptor GPR55 in inactive and active states, revealing an atypical activation mechanism. The inactive structure bound to an inverse agonist enabled rational design of an improved tool compound, BI-8310. They also found that glycosylation regulates the receptor's efficacy, providing new molecular insight into how GPR55 signaling can be modulated.

papers.title: Biochemistry of protozoan Metacaspases: Structure, processing, and inhibition.
papers.abstract: Metacaspases are calcium-dependent cysteine proteases (clan CD, family C14) present in fungi, protozoa, and plants but absent from mammals. Although structurally related to metazoan caspases, they differ in substrate specificity (cleaving after arginine or lysine), calcium-dependent activation, and monomeric architecture. In protozoan parasites such as Trypanosoma brucei, T. cruzi, Leishmania spp., Plasmodium spp., and Toxoplasma gondii, metacaspases regulate programmed cell death, cell cycle progression, protein quality control, differentiation, and virulence. Their absence in humans and esse
papers.summary: This review examines metacaspases, calcium-dependent cysteine proteases found in fungi, protozoa, and plants but not mammals, which are structurally related to caspases yet differ in substrate specificity, activation mechanism, and monomeric structure. In protozoan parasites like Trypanosoma, Leishmania, Plasmodium, and Toxoplasma, these enzymes regulate programmed cell death, cell cycle progression, protein quality control, differentiation, and virulence, making them attractive drug targets given their absence in humans.

papers.title: Structure-guided development of G protein-biased apelin receptor agonists for cardiovascular disease.
papers.abstract: Apelin receptor (APLNR) is a crucial G protein-coupled receptor that plays a central role in cardiovascular homeostasis; therefore, it represents a promising therapeutic target for heart failure, myocardial infarction, cardiac hypertrophy, and pulmonary arterial hypertension. However, the activation of APLNR simultaneously engages inhibitory G protein (Gi)-mediated protective signaling and β-arrestin pathways that are associated with pathological cardiac remodeling, thereby imposing significant limitations and challenges for the therapeutic development of conventional balanced agonists. Recent
papers.journal: Journal of Zhejiang University. Science. B
papers.summary: This paper describes the structure-guided design of apelin receptor (APLNR) agonists that preferentially activate protective G protein signaling while avoiding β-arrestin pathways linked to pathological cardiac remodeling. By exploiting structural insights into the receptor, the authors develop biased agonists with potential for treating heart failure, myocardial infarction, and pulmonary arterial hypertension. The work illustrates how biased agonism can be engineered to improve the therapeutic profile of GPCR-targeted cardiovascular drugs.

papers.title: RAF isoform selectivity of MEK inhibitors and rational design of a covalent ARAF-MEK inhibitor.
papers.abstract: Aberrant activation of the RAS/RAF/mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)/extracellular signal-regulated kinase pathway is a frequent cause of cancer. Allosteric MEK inhibitors block this pathway by binding RAF-MEK complexes to prevent activation of MEK by RAF. However, how MEK inhibitor potency varies across the three RAF isoforms remains poorly understood. We profiled seven allosteric MEK inhibitors and observed a notable hierarchy of sensitivity: All most potently inhibited CRAF-driven MEK activation while relatively sparing ARAF-driven activation. We identified point mutations in AR
papers.summary: This study profiles seven allosteric MEK inhibitors and finds a consistent sensitivity hierarchy across RAF isoforms, with CRAF-driven MEK activation most potently inhibited and ARAF-driven activation relatively spared. Using point mutations in ARAF, the authors identify determinants of this isoform selectivity and rationally design a covalent ARAF-MEK inhibitor, offering a strategy to target ARAF-specific signaling in RAS/RAF-mutant cancers.

papers.title: Evolution-Informed Viroinformatics Identifies Conserved Immune Targets with Predicted Lower Mutational Vulnerability Across Betacoronaviruses.
papers.abstract: The extensive evolutionary diversity and continuous mutational adaptation of betacoronaviruses represent a major challenge to the development of broadly protective countermeasures. This study applied an evolution-informed Viroinformatics framework to systematically identify conserved and immune targets with predicted lower mutational vulnerability across betacoronaviruses. The workflow integrated comparative sequence conservation and phylogenetic analysis with immunoinformatics-based epitope screening, HLA population coverage, mutational escape profiling, structural modeling, molecular docking
papers.summary: The study applies an evolution-informed bioinformatics pipeline to identify conserved immune targets across betacoronaviruses that are predicted to be less vulnerable to mutation. By combining sequence conservation, phylogenetics, epitope screening, HLA coverage, mutational escape profiling, and structural docking, the authors highlight candidate targets for broadly protective countermeasures. The work is a computational prioritization effort rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Metabolic Profiling, Antioxidant Activity, and Mechanistic Insights of Chicory from Northern and Southern China: Integrating Metabolomics, Machine Learning, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics Simulations, and In Vitro Assays.
papers.abstract: Chicory is a traditional food-medicinal plant, and its antioxidant efficacy has been recognized. However, the specific differences in the metabolic characteristics and antioxidant activity of chicory caused by geographical differences remain unclear. In this study, a total of 64 volatile components and 35 non-volatile components of northern and southern chicory were identified. Chemometric combined with machine learning was applied to screen 8 volatile and 7 non-volatile potential chemical biomarkers. Furthermore, the core targets of the chicory antioxidant were revealed by network pharmacolog
papers.summary: This study compared the metabolic profiles and antioxidant activity of chicory from northern and southern China, identifying 64 volatile and 35 non-volatile components and using chemometrics plus machine learning to pinpoint 8 volatile and 7 non-volatile biomarker compounds. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were then used to identify core antioxidant targets, supported by in vitro assays. The work links geographical origin to chemical composition and proposes mechanistic explanations for chicory's antioxidant effects.

papers.title: Prunus mume Extract Cooperates with Cisplatin to Induce Melanoma Apoptosis and Regulate Immune Responses.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the potential of Prunus mume (P. mume) extract as an anticancer adjuvant by evaluating its direct apoptotic effects on A375P human melanoma cells and its immunomodulatory impact on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Furthermore, the extract demonstrated additive and chemosensitizing effects when combined with a sub-toxic dose of cisplatin, significantly enhancing the growth inhibition of A375P cells. Selective growth inhibition was confirmed using crystal violet assays, where the 80% ethanol (EtOH) extract exhibited significant dose-dependent inhibition of A375
papers.summary: This study shows that an 80% ethanol extract of Prunus mume (Japanese apricot) can directly induce apoptosis in A375P melanoma cells and modulate immune responses in peripheral blood mononuclear cells. When combined with a sub-toxic dose of cisplatin, the extract produced additive and chemosensitizing effects, enhancing tumor cell growth inhibition. The findings suggest P. mume extract may serve as a natural anticancer adjuvant in melanoma therapy.

papers.title: Design, Synthesis, Evaluation, and Molecular Dynamics Simulation of Tadalafil Derivatives for the Treatment of Erectile Dysfunction.
papers.abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) remains a global health burden, yet the clinical utility of tadalafil is constrained by its poor aqueous solubility, cross-inhibition of homologous PDE isoforms, and an efficacy ceiling that cannot be overcome by dose adjustment alone. Herein, a series of diketopiperazine-based tadalafil analogues were designed and synthesized by decorating the amide nitrogen with flexible carbon chains and polar fragments (glycine, taurine, cysteine, and succinic/glutaric anhydride spacers), and by replacing the 3,4-methylenedioxybenzyl motif with substituted aromatic aldehydes. All
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of a series of tadalafil analogues intended to overcome the poor solubility and PDE-isoform selectivity limits of the parent drug for erectile dysfunction. The analogues were made by modifying the amide nitrogen with flexible carbon chains and polar groups and by swapping the methylenedioxybenzyl group for substituted aromatic aldehydes, with molecular dynamics simulations used to evaluate the compounds.

papers.title: In Silico Investigation of Candidate Anticancer Targets for Aryltetralin Lignans Previously Reported from Cleistanthus Species.
papers.abstract: Aryltetralin lignans isolated from the fruits of Cleistanthus species exhibit substantial cytotoxic activity, although the molecular interactions underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. This study combined computational target investigation with previously published experimental chemical characterization and cytotoxic evidence and no new isolation or cytotoxicity experiments were carried out. Cleistantoxin, 7-hydroxypicropolygamain, neo-cleistantoxin, cleisindoside A, cleisindoside D, and cleistonkinin D were previously isolated from C. indochinensis, C. tonkinensis, C. eberha
papers.summary: This study used computational docking and target-prediction approaches to investigate which proteins might mediate the anticancer effects of six aryltetralin lignans previously isolated from Cleistanthus species. No new experiments were performed; the work integrates prior chemical and cytotoxicity data with in silico target identification. The findings propose candidate molecular targets that could guide future experimental validation of these cytotoxic natural products.

papers.title: Thermophysically Guided Design of Spray-Dried Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Microcapsules with Improved Thermal Stability.
papers.abstract: Spray drying and gastrointestinal transit can cause substantial losses in probiotic viability, limiting effective delivery in food applications. This study developed a thermophysically guided framework for the rational design of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum microcapsules in three sequential stages. First, Kissinger kinetic analysis of eleven biopolymer candidates (Ea: 95.4-198.4 kJ/mol) combined with pH-dependent solubility profiling provided an empirical screening criterion for the preselection of coating materials; the activation energies are apparent values associated with a composite endo
papers.summary: This study presents a three-stage framework for designing spray-dried Lactiplantibacillus plantarum microcapsules with improved thermal stability. Using Kissinger kinetic analysis of eleven biopolymer candidates (activation energies 95.4–198.4 kJ/mol) combined with pH-dependent solubility profiling, the authors established an empirical screening criterion for preselection of coating materials. The approach aims to reduce probiotic viability losses during spray drying and gastrointestinal transit.

papers.title: Adhesives Inspired by Marine Organisms: Multifunctional Design and Application for Complex Wet/Underwater Environments.
papers.abstract: Achieving strong adhesion in humid or underwater environments is a long-term challenge in materials science. Water molecules form a hydration layer on the substrate surface, blocking effective contact between the adhesive and the interface, leading to the failure of traditional adhesives. The wet adhesion strength of viscoelastic materials is due to the synergistic effect of interfacial chemical bonds and multiscale energy dissipation, but water environment can seriously interfere with this mechanism. In nature, mussels, barnacles, and sandcastle worms have evolved unique wet adhesion strategi
papers.summary: This review surveys how marine organisms such as mussels, barnacles, and sandcastle worms achieve strong wet adhesion, focusing on the interplay between interfacial chemical bonding and multiscale energy dissipation that overcomes the hydration layer blocking conventional adhesives. It then discusses how these biological strategies inspire the design of multifunctional adhesives for humid and underwater environments. The work is a materials-science synthesis rather than a new experimental or computational result.

papers.title: Butein Interacts at the Minor Groove of DNA: Multi-Spectroscopic, Thermodynamic, and Bioinformatic Analyses.
papers.abstract: DNA is an important therapeutic target, and characterizing its interactions with small molecules can inform drug development. Butein is a chalcone with reported antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer activities. This study investigated the interaction between butein and calf thymus DNA using spectroscopic and computational methods. UV-visible absorption and fluorescence quenching measurements supported complex formation. Fluorescence-derived binding constants ranged from 4.04 × 103 to 5.62 × 103 M-1, indicating weak to moderate binding affinity. Thermodynamic analysis indicated spontan
papers.summary: This study characterizes how the plant-derived compound butein binds to calf thymus DNA using spectroscopy, thermodynamics, and computational modeling. The binding is weak to moderate (affinity constants ~10^3 M^-1) and occurs at the DNA minor groove, suggesting butein's reported bioactivities may involve direct DNA interaction. The work is a standard biophysical characterization of a single small molecule.

papers.title: Microbial Rhodopsins: Structural-Functional Mechanisms and the Design of Optogenetic Silencing Tools-With Emphasis on Halorubrum Archaeorhodopsins.
papers.abstract: Microbial rhodopsins are light-sensitive membrane proteins that use retinal as a covalent chromophore and adopt a seven-transmembrane α-helical fold. They are widely distributed across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi and mediate diverse functions, including light-driven ion transport, light-gated ion conduction, and photosensory signaling. Since the discovery of bacteriorhodopsin in 1971, the microbial rhodopsin family has expanded continuously, and channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics has revolutionized neuroscience by enabling millisecond-scale optical control of neuronal activity. Howeve
papers.summary: This review examines the structural and functional mechanisms of microbial rhodopsins—seven-transmembrane retinal-binding proteins found across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi—that mediate light-driven ion transport, light-gated conduction, and photosensory signaling. It traces the field from bacteriorhodopsin's discovery to channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics, with particular emphasis on Halorubrum archaeorhodopsins, and discusses how structural understanding informs the design of optogenetic silencing tools.

papers.title: Rational Design of Molecularly Imprinted Nanozymes for Selective Degradation of Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC).
papers.abstract: Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC) is an engineering thermoplastic whose recycling is hindered by its Code-7 classification and environmental BPA leaching. Here, we report water-soluble molecularly imprinted nanozymes for the selective depolymerization of BPA-PC under mild alkaline conditions. Synthesized within cross-linked surfactant micelles, the optimized nanozyme combines shape-complementary BPA-matched pockets with surface basicity, achieving a 72-fold rate enhancement over porcine pancreatic lipase. Fluorescence titrations with a soluble dansyl-labeled BPA-PC dimer confirm strong subs
papers.summary: The authors designed water-soluble molecularly imprinted nanozymes that selectively depolymerize poly(bisphenol A carbonate) under mild alkaline conditions. The optimized nanozyme combines BPA-shaped binding pockets with surface basicity and achieves a 72-fold rate enhancement over porcine pancreatic lipase. This offers a potential route for recycling a hard-to-recycle plastic and reducing environmental BPA leaching.

papers.title: Rationally Designed Phenyl- and Phenanthryl-Based Imidazole Hybrids for the Treatment of Breast Cancer-A Structure-Activity Relationship Study.
papers.abstract: A series of 11 compounds of phenyl-imidazole-pyrrole and 9 compounds of phenanthryl-imidazole-pyrrole were synthesized and evaluated against breast cancer cell lines differing in the expression of estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor (HER)-2, viz., BT-474 (ER+, PR+, and HER2+), T-47D and MCF-7 (ER+, PR+, and HER2-), and MDA-MB-468 and MDA-MB-231 (ER-, PR-, and HER2-). The analysis of the results indicated that the most active compounds were 5d and 5k from the phenyl-imidazole-pyrrole series and 6b and 6i from the phenanthryl-imidazole-py
papers.summary: The authors synthesized and tested 20 new phenyl- and phenanthryl-imidazole-pyrrole hybrid compounds against five breast cancer cell lines with different receptor profiles (ER/PR/HER2 positive and negative). Several compounds, notably 5d, 5k, 6b, and 6i, showed the strongest activity, and the structure-activity relationships across the series were analyzed. This is an early-stage medicinal chemistry study identifying lead compounds for further anticancer development.

papers.title: Targeting FTSJ1 to Restore TP53 Function in Nonsense Mutation-Driven Cancer: Computational and Experimental Evaluation of 1,2,4-Triazole Derivatives.
papers.abstract: Nonsense mutations introduce premature termination codons (PTCs) into mRNA transcripts, leading to truncated and non-functional proteins, and accounting for approximately 10-15% of genetic disorders. In this context, the induction of translational readthrough by small molecules, known as translational readthrough-inducing drugs (TRIDs), has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy to restore full-length protein expression. However, the mechanism of action of TRIDs is still under debate, and one emerging target is FTSJ1, a methyltransferase involved in tRNA modification. FTSJ1 regulates tran
papers.summary: This study investigates small-molecule 1,2,4-triazole derivatives designed to inhibit FTSJ1, a tRNA methyltransferase, in order to promote translational readthrough of nonsense mutations and restore full-length TP53 protein in cancer cells. The work combines computational docking and screening with experimental validation, proposing FTSJ1 as a target for translational readthrough-inducing drugs (TRIDs). It offers a potential therapeutic strategy for the ~10-15% of genetic disorders and cancers driven by premature termination codons.

papers.title: Pyridine-3-Carboxamide-1,3,4-Thiadiazole Hybrids as Antimicrobial Agents: Synthesis, Biological Evaluation, In Vivo Toxicity, and Computational Studies.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance necessitates the development of novel antimicrobial agents with improved efficacy and favorable safety profiles. In this study, a new series of pyridine-3-carboxamide-1,3,4-thiadiazole hybrids and their corresponding N-Mannich bases bearing structurally diverse piperazine substituents were designed, synthesized, and characterized by FT-IR, 1H/13C NMR, and HR-MS. Their antimicrobial activity was evaluated against reference and clinical bacterial and fungal strains using broth microdilution and agar diffusion assays. The compounds exhibited selecti
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of new pyridine-3-carboxamide-1,3,4-thiadiazole hybrids and their N-Mannich base derivatives, which were tested for antimicrobial activity against bacterial and fungal strains. The compounds showed selective antimicrobial effects, and the study also included in vivo toxicity assessment and computational (docking) studies to support the findings. The work aims to address antimicrobial resistance by identifying new lead compounds with favorable safety profiles.

papers.title: From whole-exome sequencing to functional insight: Characterization of rare germline variants in lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) has greatly expanded the identification of rare germline variants in hereditary cancer predisposition. However, the interpretation of variants of uncertain significance (VUS), particularly in novel candidate genes, remains a major challenge in lung cancer genetics.
papers.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of interpreting rare germline variants of uncertain significance (VUS) identified through whole-exome sequencing in lung cancer patients. It moves beyond variant discovery toward functional characterization of variants in novel candidate predisposition genes, aiming to bridge the gap between WES findings and clinical interpretation.

papers.title: Designing Cooperative Molecular Glues for FKBP12-MAPRE1 with Enhanced-Sampling Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Molecular glues (MGs) offer a unique modality for inducing protein-protein interactions (PPIs), yet their rational design is often hindered by the limitations of static structural data. Here, we present a computational pipeline for the design of cooperative MGs for the FKBP12-MAPRE1 system using replica exchange with solute scaling (REST2) for enhanced sampling in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. By sampling the conformational ensembles of binary and ternary complexes, we identified a "stabilized configurational space" that facilitates ternary-complex formation through a combination of con
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: The authors develop a computational pipeline that uses enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics (REST2) to design cooperative molecular glues that induce the FKBP12–MAPRE1 protein–protein interaction. By sampling conformational ensembles of binary and ternary complexes, they identify a 'stabilized configurational space' that promotes ternary-complex formation through combined conformational effects. This offers a rational design strategy for molecular glues beyond static structural data.

papers.title: Dietary Curcumin Protects Common Carp (Cyprinus carpio) Against Potassium Permanganate-Induced Toxicity: Hematological, Immunological, Oxidative, and Molecular Docking Evidence.
papers.abstract: Potassium permanganate treatment can adversely affect fish physiology despite its usefulness in aquaculture. This study evaluated the protective effects of dietary curcumin against potassium permanganate-induced disturbances in common carp (Cyprinus carpio). Fish were fed a basal diet or diets supplemented with 1%, 2%, or 4% curcumin for eight weeks, with or without subsequent exposure to potassium permanganate at 2 mg/L for 30 min daily for seven days. Hematological and immune parameters and oxidative status in the liver, kidney, spleen, and gill were assessed. Potassium permanganate exposure
papers.summary: This study shows that feeding common carp a curcumin-supplemented diet (1–4%) for eight weeks reduces the hematological, immunological, and oxidative damage caused by potassium permanganate exposure, a common aquaculture disinfectant. Molecular docking evidence is also presented to support curcumin's protective mechanism. The work suggests dietary curcumin could be a practical protective additive in aquaculture settings where potassium permanganate is used.

papers.title: A Dipeptide Module Substitution-Based Strategy for the Modification and Evaluation of ACE Inhibitory Peptides.
papers.abstract: Food-derived angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitory peptide LYPVK exhibits promising potential for application as an important ingredient with a potential antihypertensive effect in functional foods. However, the structure-activity relationship and the rational design strategy for peptide modification remain insufficiently understood. To address this, dipeptide module substitution was employed to modify and investigate the mechanism of this food-derived ACE inhibitory peptide, providing an insight into the structure-activity relationship. Through integration of molecular docking and ac
papers.summary: This study introduces a dipeptide module substitution strategy to modify the food-derived ACE inhibitory peptide LYPVK, aiming to clarify its structure-activity relationship. By combining molecular docking with activity assays, the authors identify key dipeptide modules that influence ACE inhibition, enabling rational design of improved antihypertensive peptides for functional foods.

papers.title: Food-Derived Umami Peptides: Linking Candidate Discovery, Experimental Validation, and Food Applications.
papers.abstract: Alternative proteins and cultivated meat increase the need for flavour strategies that maintain savoury quality with less reliance on salt and conventional seasonings. Food-derived umami peptides are promising candidates, but their practical value depends on evidence beyond sequence prediction. With advances in virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted approaches, discovery is expanding from sensory-guided preparation toward candidate-library construction and data-driven prioritization. This review compares food-protein resources and experimental and sequence-based discovery routes, and
papers.summary: This review examines how food-derived umami peptides are discovered and validated, comparing traditional sensory-guided approaches with newer computational routes such as virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted candidate prioritization. It highlights that practical value depends on experimental evidence beyond sequence prediction, and surveys food-protein resources and validation strategies relevant to reducing salt and conventional seasoning reliance in alternative proteins and cultivated meat.

papers.title: C-RAF Sequence-Encoded Cooperativity Hotspots for 14-3-3/C-RAF Molecular Glues.
papers.abstract: 14-3-3 Proteins are hub proteins with an extensive interactome of phosphorylated client proteins, making them attractive targets for molecular glues (MGs) that stabilize specific 14-3-3/client protein complexes. However, selectively stabilizing individual 14-3-3 protein-protein interactions (PPIs) remains a key challenge for effectively drugging the 14-3-3 interactome. Here, we systematically investigated the sequence-encoded determinants underlying selective stabilization of the 14-3-3/C-RAF complex by covalent MGs. Using stepwise C-terminal peptide sequence extension, alanine scanning, and M
papers.summary: This study systematically dissects how the amino acid sequence of the C-RAF C-terminus encodes selectivity for 14-3-3/C-RAF molecular glues, using stepwise peptide extension and alanine scanning. The authors identify sequence-encoded cooperativity hotspots that determine whether a covalent molecular glue can selectively stabilize this specific 14-3-3 protein-protein interaction. These findings provide a blueprint for designing selective molecular glues targeting individual 14-3-3 complexes.

papers.title: A Generalized Theory for the Structural and Spatial Mapping of Energy, Entropy, and Free Energy.
papers.abstract: Systems in which the free energy density is nonuniform in space are familiar; the surface tension of a water droplet and the surface energy of a solid are good examples. Some such cases can be treated with prior theory, notably inhomogeneous solvation theory (IST), but IST is applicable only to liquids. Despite this limitation, IST has proven useful as a guide to the design of ligands to bind a targeted protein, based on the idea that ligands that displace high free energy water will tend to bind more tightly, other things being equal. Here, we present Generalized Thermodynamic Mapping (GTM) t
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.summary: The authors introduce Generalized Thermodynamic Mapping (GTM), a theoretical framework that extends inhomogeneous solvation theory (previously limited to liquids) to map energy, entropy, and free energy in both structural and spatial contexts for arbitrary systems. This generalizes the analysis of nonuniform free energy density, with potential applications such as ligand design where displacing high-free-energy water improves binding.

papers.title: Stoichiometry-dependent gating and structural pharmacology of cardiac GIRK1/4 channels.
papers.abstract: Cardiac G protein-gated inwardly rectifying potassium-K + (GIRK) channels, formed by GIRK1/4 heterotetramers or GIRK4 homotetramers, are crucial regulators of heart rate, and their dysfunction is associated with atrial fibrillation. Despite their therapeutic potential as anti-arrhythmic targets, development of selective GIRK modulators has been limited by an incomplete understanding of their structures, gating mechanisms, and pharmacology. Here, we report high-resolution structures of the GIRK4 homotetramer and of GIRK1/4 heterotetramers, revealing that they form in unexpected 1:3 and 2:2 asse
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study presents high-resolution cryo-EM structures of cardiac GIRK channels, revealing that GIRK1/4 heterotetramers assemble in unexpected 1:3 and 2:2 stoichiometries rather than the assumed 2:2 arrangement. The structures show that subunit stoichiometry influences channel gating and pharmacology, providing a structural basis for developing selective anti-arrhythmic drugs targeting these channels in atrial fibrillation.

papers.title: PepRePs: Peptide-Retargeted Phosphatases Designed with Generative Language Models.
papers.abstract: Phosphorylation is a fast, reversible layer of post-translational control that directly governs protein activity, signaling flux, and cell state. Kinases and phosphatases collectively establish these phosphorylation states, but their dysregulation drives cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, and developmental disorders. Selectively manipulating the phosphorylation of individual proteins in cells remains challenging, particularly for disordered substrates. Here, we introduce Pep tide- Re targeted P hosphatase s ( PepRePs ), a genetically encoded system that fuses a peptide binder to a serine/thre
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce PepRePs, a genetically encoded system that retargets serine/threonine phosphatases to specific substrate proteins by fusing them to peptide binders. This enables selective manipulation of phosphorylation on individual proteins in cells, including disordered substrates that are otherwise difficult to target. The peptide binders were designed using generative language models, offering a general strategy for controlling post-translational signaling with precision.

papers.title: Functional Consequence of IRF6 Variants in Van der Woude Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Van der Woude syndrome (VWS) is the most common syndromic form of orofacial clefts (OFCs). The heritability of VWS is largely (~70%) explained by variants in the IRF6 gene. Experimental studies to confirm genetic variant effects are essential but are time intensive and expensive. Advancing next-generation sequencing techniques has made it possible to identify genetic variation quicker than their causal effects in disease processes can be ascertained. Therefore, employing computational tools to reliably predict their causal effects is crucial for advancing translational research. We conducted S
papers.summary: This study applies computational prediction tools to assess the functional consequences of IRF6 variants associated with Van der Woude syndrome, the most common syndromic form of orofacial clefts. The authors aim to prioritize which genetic variants are likely to be causal, addressing the gap between rapid variant discovery by next-generation sequencing and the slower experimental validation of variant effects. The work supports translational research by providing a computational framework for interpreting IRF6 variants.

papers.title: Application of computational methods in the drug discovery and development of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder marked by the accumulation of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles in the brain, leading to cognitive decline. As the most common dementia, AD affects over 50 million individuals worldwide, with 10 million new cases each year. Despite many significant progresses in AD research fields, there is still no effective treatment. Advances in molecular modelling and artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm have facilitated the application of computational methods in AD drug development, offering advantages in terms of efficiency,
papers.summary: This review surveys how computational approaches—molecular modeling and AI algorithms—are being applied to Alzheimer's disease drug discovery and development, from target identification through lead optimization. Given the disease's enormous global burden and the persistent lack of effective treatments, the authors argue these methods offer efficiency advantages over traditional experimental pipelines. The paper serves as an overview of the current computational toolkit for AD therapeutics rather than presenting new primary results.

papers.title: Structural basis for inhibition of the lipid flippase MurJ by phage lysis protein SglPP7 suggests convergent evolution with other Sgl peptides.
papers.abstract: Some bacteriophages encode lysis proteins that inhibit essential bacterial processes, and elucidating their mechanisms is valuable for developing antibacterial strategies against drug-resistant pathogens. We determined the cryo-EM structure of the complex between the essential Escherichia coli lipid II flippase MurJ and the phage lysis protein SglPP7. Structural, mutational, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation analyses revealed that SglPP7 binds along the intramembrane cleft of MurJ and inserts its C-terminal tail into the internal cavity, stabilizing MurJ in an outward-facing conformation.
papers.summary: This study reports the cryo-EM structure of the E. coli lipid II flippase MurJ bound to the phage lysis protein SglPP7. SglPP7 inserts its C-terminal tail into MurJ's internal cavity and stabilizes an outward-facing conformation, inhibiting the flippase. Comparisons suggest this inhibition mechanism evolved convergently with other Sgl peptides, offering a structural template for antibacterial strategies.

papers.title: Integrative Machine Learning and Immunoinformatics-Guided Design and In Silico Validation of a Multiepitope DNA Vaccine Against Avian Metapneumovirus.
papers.abstract: Avian metapneumovirus (aMPV) is an emerging viral pathogen causing many outbreaks in chickens all over the world. There are several subtypes of the MPV circulating in chickens in the US. The current circulating subtypes of the virus in the US chicken are A, B, and C. Despite the availability of some aMPV vaccines in the US, most of these vaccines are based on foreign strains, particularly European aMPV-A/B strains. Their protective efficacy against contemporary U.S. aMPV isolates has not been fully established. The main goal of this study is to integrate the most recent aMPV genome sequencing
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning and immunoinformatics to design a multiepitope DNA vaccine against avian metapneumovirus (aMPV), targeting multiple circulating subtypes (A, B, and C) found in U.S. chickens. The vaccine construct was validated entirely through in silico methods, including epitope prediction and computational immune simulation, rather than experimental testing. The work addresses the limited efficacy of current vaccines based on European strains against contemporary U.S. isolates.

papers.title: Antibody peptide conjugates as multifunctional therapeutics: Mechanisms, challenges, and prospects.
papers.abstract: Antibody peptide conjugates (APCs) represent a newly emerging class of targeted biotherapeutics that embody a novel structural paradigm by combining the precise targeting capabilities of antibodies with the versatile biological functions of peptides. APCs not only overcome the inherent limitations of conventional peptide therapeutics but also go beyond the cytotoxicity-focused paradigm of traditional antibody drug conjugates (ADCs). By flexibly combining peptide payload activities with antibody functions, APCs have developed into diverse therapeutic strategies, including immunomodulation, targ
papers.summary: This review introduces antibody peptide conjugates (APCs) as an emerging class of targeted biotherapeutics that combine antibodies' precise targeting with peptides' versatile biological functions. Unlike traditional antibody-drug conjugates that focus on cytotoxicity, APCs enable diverse strategies such as immunomodulation and other peptide-driven mechanisms. The paper discusses the mechanisms, design challenges, and future prospects of this new therapeutic paradigm.

papers.title: BD2-selective BRD4 inhibitor ZX29 mitigates myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury via BRD4-YY1-NCOA4 axis disruption and ferroptosis inhibition.
papers.abstract: Myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (MI/RI) remains a major barrier to ischemic heart disease treatment, as reperfusion therapies often exacerbate cardiac damage. Bromodomain-containing protein 4 (BRD4) is a key epigenetic target in cardiovascular diseases, but pan-BRD4 inhibitors cause severe off-target toxicity by disrupting basal bromodomain 1 (BD1) function, highlighting the need for BD2-selective agents. This study aimed to develop a BD2-selective BRD4 inhibitor and clarify its mechanism. ZX29 was developed via virtual screening of 100,000 compounds and structure-based optimization, ex
papers.summary: The authors developed ZX29, a BD2-selective BRD4 inhibitor, through virtual screening and structure-based optimization, to avoid the toxicity of pan-BRD4 inhibitors that also block BD1. ZX29 was shown to mitigate myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury by disrupting a BRD4-YY1-NCOA4 axis and inhibiting ferroptosis. This identifies BD2-selective BRD4 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy for cardiac reperfusion damage.

papers.title: Drugging the "undruggable" p53: a structure-guided strategy against the Y220C mutation.
papers.abstract: Tumor Protein p53 (TP53) is the most frequently altered gene in human cancer, yet mutant p53 has long been considered undruggable. The Y220C mutation is exceptional because it both destabilizes the p53 DNA-binding domain (DBD) and creates a unique surface pocket absent in wild-type protein. Availability of structural information enabled structure-based development of rezatapopt (PC14586), which binds this neo-pocket, stabilizes mutant p53, and restores transcriptional tumor suppressor activity. Early clinical studies in the PYNNACLE trial provide proof-of-concept efficacy and reveal emerging o
papers.summary: This review discusses structure-guided strategies to target the p53 Y220C mutation, which creates a unique surface pocket absent in wild-type p53. The drug rezatapopt (PC14586) binds this neo-pocket, stabilizes mutant p53, and restores its tumor suppressor function. Early clinical data from the PYNNACLE trial provide proof-of-concept efficacy for this approach against a previously 'undruggable' target.

papers.title: Structure-Based Design and Biological Evaluation of Imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine Derivatives as Potential Antituberculosis Agents.
papers.abstract: A library of 11 novel imidazopyridine-based sulfonamide derivatives (4a-4k) were synthesized through the coupling of an imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine hydrochloride intermediate with various substituted sulfonyl chloride derivatives (3a-3k). The structures of the compounds (4a-4k) were confirmed using appropriate spectroscopic techniques. The synthesized derivatives (4a-4k) were subsequently evaluated for their antitubercular and antioxidant potential. Among the tested molecules, compounds 4b, 4d, and 4g demonstrated moderate antimycobacterial activity, displaying minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a library of 11 imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine sulfonamide derivatives and tested them for antitubercular and antioxidant activity. Three compounds (4b, 4d, 4g) showed moderate antimycobacterial activity, though the abstract does not report specific MIC values or structural rationale.

papers.title: SprintX: mitigating data scarcity in antibody design via synthetic structural prior knowledge dataset.
papers.abstract: Structure-based artificial intelligence (AI)-driven antibody design is increasingly important for therapeutic development, yet progress has been hindered by the scarcity of high-quality antibody-antigen complex structures for model training. To alleviate this bottleneck, we introduce SprintX (Structural Prior for Antibody-Antigen CompleXes), a large-scale AlphaFold3-derived synthetic dataset designed to provide structural prior knowledge for antibody-antigen modeling. Unlike conventional docking-based synthesis pipelines, SprintX uses AlphaFold3 to generate antigen-conditioned candidate comple
papers.summary: SprintX is a large-scale synthetic dataset of antibody-antigen complex structures generated using AlphaFold3, designed to address the scarcity of experimental structures available for training AI antibody design models. Unlike docking-based approaches, it produces antigen-conditioned candidate complexes, providing structural prior knowledge that can be used to pretrain or augment models for antibody-antigen modeling. The work aims to lower the data bottleneck hindering structure-based therapeutic antibody development.

papers.title: Integrative genomic SEM analysis of shared genetic architecture and candidate genes for insulin resistance-related metabolic traits.
papers.abstract: Insulin resistance is a complex metabolic state involving impaired insulin sensitivity, compensatory insulin secretion, abnormal lipid metabolism, and altered fat distribution. However, the shared genetic architecture underlying these correlated phenotypes remains incompletely defined. In this study, we applied Genomic Structural Equation Modeling to genome-wide association summary statistics of fasting insulin, insulin sensitivity index, triglycerides, and waist-to-hip ratio to construct an insulin resistance-related latent genetic factor. SNP-level association analysis was then performed for
papers.summary: This study applied genomic structural equation modeling to GWAS summary statistics for fasting insulin, insulin sensitivity index, triglycerides, and waist-to-hip ratio to construct a latent genetic factor representing insulin resistance. The authors then performed SNP-level association analysis on this latent factor to identify shared genetic architecture and candidate genes underlying insulin resistance-related metabolic traits. The work provides a framework for understanding the common genetic basis of correlated metabolic phenotypes.

papers.title: 1-Methylhistidine attenuates early myocardial inflammation in type 3 cardiorenal syndrome through modulation of the p105/p50 NF-κB axis.
papers.abstract: Type 3 cardiorenal syndrome (CRS3) is characterized by cardiac injury or dysfunction secondary to acute kidney injury (AKI), yet the contribution of AKI-associated metabolic remodeling to early myocardial inflammation remains poorly understood. Here, paired serum and myocardial untargeted metabolomics identified 1-methylhistidine (1-MH) as a metabolite elevated in both compartments, with the highest variable importance in projection score in serum. Exogenous 1-MH improved the E/A ratio and attenuated myocardial inflammation and terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick-end labeling (TUNE
papers.summary: Using paired serum and heart-tissue metabolomics in a type 3 cardiorenal syndrome model, the authors identified 1-methylhistidine as a metabolite elevated in both compartments after acute kidney injury. Exogenous 1-methylhistidine improved cardiac diastolic function (E/A ratio) and reduced myocardial inflammation and apoptosis, apparently by modulating the p105/p50 NF-κB axis. This suggests a metabolite-mediated link between kidney injury and early cardiac inflammation.

papers.title: Teaching computational toxicology as new approach methodologies in the era of next-generation risk assessment.
papers.abstract: The global initiative toward non-animal chemical testing methods has recently gained significant momentum, requiring developing new approach methodologies (NAMs) as transformative solutions for next-generation risk assessment (NGRA). NAMs refer to any in chemico, in silico, and in vitro technology, methodology, or combination that do not rely on animals. A range of computational toxicology methods are becoming critical components within the NGRA framework across multiple testing tiers. These approaches are needed to support hazard characterization and prioritization for further testing, calcul
papers.summary: This perspective article argues that computational toxicology methods should be taught as core new approach methodologies (NAMs) within next-generation risk assessment (NGRA) frameworks, which aim to replace animal testing with in silico, in chemico, and in vitro approaches. It outlines how computational tools support hazard characterization and chemical prioritization across testing tiers, and discusses educational strategies for training the next generation of toxicologists in these methods.

papers.title: Research progress on the application of multi-scale computational methods in the research and development of anti-tuberculosis infection drugs.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), driven by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading cause of mortality from infectious disease worldwide.​ The global dissemination of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains-coupled with protracted treatment regimens and the persistence of latent infection-has not only compromised first-line chemotherapies but also underscored the stagnation of conventional drug development pipelines. In this review, we systematically synthesize how multi-scale computational strategies are reshaping anti-TB drug discovery and explicitly delineate the
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how multi-scale computational methods—spanning molecular modeling, network analysis, and systems-level approaches—are being applied to anti-tuberculosis drug discovery. It highlights how these strategies address the stagnation of conventional pipelines amid rising multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant Mtb strains. The paper frames computational integration as a way to accelerate target identification and drug development for TB.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic and computational analysis associates Ms4a6c+ macrophages with fibrosis in radiation proctitis and computationally nominates MOTS-c as a candidate modulator.
papers.abstract: Chronic radiation proctitis (CRP) represents a significant clinical challenge characterized by irreversible fibrosis and a lack of specific pharmacological interventions. This study aimed to elucidate the cellular mechanisms underlying impaired tissue repair to identify novel therapeutic targets.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic profiling with computational analyses to identify Ms4a6c+ macrophages as a cell population associated with fibrosis in chronic radiation proctitis. The authors then use computational approaches to nominate MOTS-c as a candidate modulator of this fibrotic process. The work is exploratory and hypothesis-generating, with the macrophage-fibrosis association and MOTS-c nomination remaining to be validated experimentally.

papers.title: A dual-function XCL1-CD40L mRNA adjuvant potentiates cancer vaccines by coordinating DC recruitment and maturation.
papers.abstract: Despite the significant promise of mRNA tumor vaccines in treating solid tumors, their clinical response rate is constrained by the low effectiveness of antigen presentation resulting from the immune-suppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Conventional type 1 dendritic cells (cDC1) are pivotal in antigen cross-presentation; yet, they frequently exhibit insufficient immune-activating communication within solid malignancies.
papers.summary: This paper describes a dual-function mRNA adjuvant encoding XCL1 and CD40L that is designed to improve cancer vaccine efficacy. XCL1 recruits conventional type 1 dendritic cells (cDC1) into the tumor microenvironment, while CD40L promotes their maturation, together enhancing antigen cross-presentation. The approach addresses the immunosuppressive TME that limits current mRNA tumor vaccines.

papers.title: Transcriptomic identification of high-altitude illness candidate genes and physiological mechanisms: a multidimensional bioinformatics study with 106 drug-food homologous substance target prediction.
papers.abstract: High-altitude (HA) illness threatens health after acute high-altitude exposure, but its molecular mechanisms and effective interventions remain unclear. Drug-food homologous (DFH) substances have potential for HA illness intervention, yet their active components and targets are unknown.
papers.summary: This study uses transcriptomic and bioinformatics analyses to identify candidate genes underlying high-altitude illness and predicts targets of 106 drug-food homologous substances as potential interventions. It aims to link molecular mechanisms of altitude sickness to natural compounds that might mitigate it.

papers.title: Machine learning, molecular docking, and experimental validation identify shared molecular signatures between idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and malignant pleural mesothelioma: a retrospective study.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) exhibits cancer-like features, yet its pathogenesis remains unclear. Given molecular similarities between IPAH and malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM), this study aimed to uncover shared transcriptomic patterns.
papers.summary: This study used machine learning and molecular docking, followed by experimental validation, to identify shared transcriptomic signatures between idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) and malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM). The authors report overlapping molecular patterns that may help explain the cancer-like features of IPAH and suggest common pathways for further investigation.

papers.title: Unleashing the industrial potential of microbial plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes: recent advances in protein engineering.
papers.abstract: Plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes (PCWPEs) used in industry are predominantly of microbial origin. Key enzyme classes, including cellulases, lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases (LPMOs), β-xylanases, β-mannanases and pectinases, have attained technological maturity and are widely deployed across agro-waste biorefineries, food and feed processing, textile and pulp manufacturing. Low catalytic efficiency, insufficient thermostability, poor operational adaptability, restricted functionality, and product inhibition limit the industrial use of these enzymes. Structure- and sequence-gu
papers.summary: This review surveys protein engineering strategies for improving microbial plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes (cellulases, LPMOs, xylanases, mannanases, pectinases) used in biorefineries, food/feed processing, textiles, and pulp manufacturing. It highlights how structure- and sequence-guided engineering can address limitations such as low catalytic efficiency, poor thermostability, and product inhibition to enhance industrial performance.

papers.title: Tailoring plant-based food emulsions with oil bodies and proteins recovered by alkali aqueous extraction from rapeseed (Brassica napus L.) oilseeds.
papers.abstract: Oil bodies (OBs) and storage proteins recovered from oilseeds by aqueous extraction are promising ingredients for the development of plant-based food emulsions. This study aimed to co-extract natural OBs and storage proteins from rapeseed oilseeds, to explore the microstructure, to analyse the composition, to investigate the emulsifying properties of the proteins and to determine the impact of pH on the physical stability of natural OBs, homogenized OBs, proteins and protein-stabilized oil droplets in emulsions. Alkali aqueous extraction at pH 9.5 enabled the recovery of well-dispersed OBs tog
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that oil bodies and storage proteins can be co-extracted from rapeseed using alkaline aqueous extraction at pH 9.5, yielding well-dispersed oil bodies suitable for plant-based food emulsions. The authors characterize the microstructure and composition of the extracts and evaluate how pH affects the physical stability of natural oil bodies, homogenized oil bodies, proteins, and protein-stabilized oil droplets in emulsions. The work provides practical insight into using these co-extracted ingredients to tailor emulsion stability for plant-based food applications.

papers.title: Exploring molecular interactions between yeast topoisomerase I and RNA polymerase III subunit, Rpc82 using an in-silico approach.
papers.abstract: The process of DNA transcription leads to the generation of torsional stress, which must be resolved for smooth progression of the transcription machinery. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, DNA topoisomerase I (Top I), a type IB topoisomerase, plays a critical role in relaxing supercoils and mitigating the topological strain associated with transcription. While several proteins from the transcription machinery have been reported to interact with yeast Top I, the precise structural domains involved and the detailed features of the interaction interfaces remain largely unexplored. This gap is partly
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and molecular dynamics to model how yeast topoisomerase I (Top I) may physically interact with Rpc82, a subunit of RNA polymerase III. The authors identify putative interaction interfaces and structural domains that could mediate this binding, offering hypotheses for how Top I is recruited to relieve torsional stress during Pol III transcription. The work is purely in-silico and provides predictions that require experimental validation.
